description: Sabemos improvisar, hablar y aceptamos desafíos
summary: AEON-01 is a browser game where players design, manage and fly a complete crewed mission from Earth orbit to the surface of Mars. Mission design is usually taught as formulas; students rarely get to feel how mass, budget, power, fuel and time fight each other. In AEON-01 the player builds a ship by choosing a launcher, 6 systems and 4 science instruments inside a 3,500 M$ budget and the launcher's payload limit, then flies it: launch to orbit at 7.8 km/s, a 210-day cruise with critical events, and entry, descent and landing on Mars. Every early choice has visible consequences months later. The physics uses real NASA numbers (NSSDCA Earth and Mars fact sheets, the Mars 2020 Perseverance landing press kit, Saturn V payload data) and the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation applied to the player's own ship mass. A final report grades each mission segment and gives an efficiency score. It runs in any web browser with no install or account, and the source code is public, so students, beginners and educators can use it freely.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
AEON-01 is a single-mission space simulator played in four stages:
1) Design – In the launch hangar the player picks a rocket and 6 ship systems (hull, tanks, life support, power, lander, heat shield) plus 4 science instruments, staying inside a 3,500 M$ budget and the launcher's payload limit.
2) Launch – From the cockpit, the player runs the countdown and flies the ascent to orbit at 7.8 km/s while watching fuel, dynamic pressure and structural integrity.
3) Cruise – During a 210-day trip the player walks a 6-room ship, refills resources, looks after the crew and decides 3 critical events, such as a solar storm.
4) Land – Atmospheric entry, parachute and retrorockets, with the goal of touching down under 4 m/s.
A final report grades the four mission segments and gives an efficiency score (science 35%, propellant 20%, heat shield 20%, oxygen 15%, decisions 10%).

HOW IT WORKS
One constants file feeds every phase, so no number is hard-coded elsewhere. Delta-v is computed with the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation from the player's own ship mass. Key values come from NASA sources: 3.6 km/s trans-Mars injection burn, a 210-day cruise modelled on Perseverance (203 days), 5.5 km/s Mars entry speed starting at 125 km, about 1,300 °C peak heat-shield temperature, parachute deployment at 11 km and 420 m/s, and Mars gravity of 3.71 m/s².

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT
Engineering trade-offs become decisions the player feels, not formulas on a page. The game runs in any web browser with no install and no account, which removes the barrier for students, beginners and educators without access to mission-design tools. The full source code is public.

TOOLS
HTML, Tailwind CSS and JavaScript (Canvas and SVG graphics), hosted on GitHub Pages. Music by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0.

CREATIVITY
Instead of menus and spreadsheets, the player lives the mission: a cockpit view for launch, a walkable ship interior, an exterior drone camera, and a customizable rocket with colors, decals and a ship name.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED
Scientific accuracy versus playability for beginners and youth, clear feedback on every decision, and accessibility on ordinary computers.

USE OF AI
Claude (Anthropic) was used for code architecture, structure and code generation. Google Gemini was used for research and data structuring. All AI-assisted code is acknowledged here and in the project repository.

NEXT STEPS
Moon and deep-space missions, live NASA space-weather data for the solar-storm event, and a Spanish classroom mode with teacher guides for schools in Paraguay.

TEAM 7 – Space Apps Encarnación
Alexander González (Game Design), Hugo Octavio (Lead Programming), Areli Gómez (UI/UX Animation), Jose Cubilla (Scientific Research).
